stories.head: How to vet AI capabilities during martech RFPs
stories.plain: Six pointed questions help buyers separate genuine AI capability from rebranded automation during vendor selection. This matters because purchasing decisions lock in platforms for years, and most vendors are overclaiming right now. Any marketer sitting through a demo or writing an RFP this budget season needs this filter.

stories.head: DXL deploys Meta's AI agent Muse via commercetools for product discovery
stories.plain: Destination XL, the largest big-and-tall menswear retailer in the US, is now selling through Meta's agentic shopping assistant Muse. This is an early live example of a major retailer routing commerce through a third-party AI agent — a structural shift in how products get discovered and bought that marketers need to track.

stories.head: What's missing from your 2027 marketing AI budget?
stories.plain: Most 2027 AI budgets fund tools but underfund the people and change-management processes that make tools work. This piece argues that adoption and governance costs are routinely left out of planning cycles, leaving teams with software they can't use. Directly relevant to anyone finalising next-year spend right now.

stories.head: fraud0 and FouAnalytics partner to offer impression-level ad governance as DoubleVerify alternative
stories.plain: Two independent ad-verification firms are combining to give advertisers AI-powered, impression-level fraud detection with automatic Google Ads refunds — positioning directly against incumbents DoubleVerify and IAS. This signals growing competition in the media governance layer and new options for marketers worried about bot traffic eating budgets.

stories.head: adMarketplace AI Discovery shows 156% conversion lift and distinct behavior across AI search surfaces
stories.plain: A full year of real data from adMarketplace's AI Discovery product finds conversion rates 156% higher than standard search, but also that consumer intent and product interest differ significantly across browsers, comparison engines, and BNPL apps. This is rare empirical evidence about how AI search surfaces fragment audience behavior — critical for media planning.

stories.head: How to vet AI capabilities during martech RFPs
stories.plain: Six practical questions help buyers separate genuine AI capability from rebranded automation during vendor selection. This matters because marketing teams are spending real budget on tools that may deliver little beyond a fresh label — and a structured RFP checklist directly changes how AI is bought and evaluated.

stories.head: DXL deploys Meta's AI agent Muse via commercetools for product discovery
stories.plain: Destination XL is the first major apparel retailer to open a commerce channel through Meta's agentic shopping AI, Muse. This is a concrete case of an AI agent acting as a sales channel — not just a chatbot — signalling how agentic decisioning is reshaping where and how products get discovered and bought.

stories.head: What's missing from your 2027 marketing AI budget?
stories.plain: Most AI budgets fund tools but skip the people, training, and processes needed to make them work. This piece offers a framework for funding AI adoption — not just AI access, directly shaping how marketing teams plan spending and governance going into the next annual cycle.

stories.head: Why a citation in an AI answer isn't the same as a recommendation — ZeroRank CEO
stories.plain: ZeroRank's CEO draws a sharp line between being mentioned and being recommended by an AI engine — a distinction most marketers currently ignore. The interview gives practical guidance on measuring real AI visibility vs. vanity citations and how to make the case to a CFO, which matters as GEO budgets are being set.

stories.head: The hidden risks of auto-generated creative: brand, legal, and regulatory exposure
stories.plain: AI-generated copy and images carry copyright liability, false-advertising risk, and data-breach exposure that many marketing teams haven't planned for. As generative AI becomes standard in content workflows, understanding these legal guardrails is essential before publishing — directly shaping how AI creative is governed and approved.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Rewriting the Purchase Path
body: When AI agents begin shortlisting B2B vendors or steering shoppers toward products, the old rules of visibility collapse. Getting cited by an AI is not the same as earning a recommendation — a distinction that upends both SEO and paid-media assumptions built over two decades.

Retailers like DXL are already deploying Meta's AI agent Muse to extend customer reach, while marketers are warned that AI agents make CX marketing's problem — meaning responsibility for the experience now sits squarely with marketing operations, not just IT or product.

themes.head: Brand & Legal Risk Hidden Inside AI Creative
body: Auto-generated creative is moving faster than the governance frameworks meant to contain it. Brand, legal, and regulatory exposure from AI-produced assets — think IP conflicts, hallucinated claims, and regulatory non-compliance — is being systematically underestimated inside marketing teams.

Enterprise governance policies alone are insufficient; the Five9 perspective crystallises it: your brand is now your AI's behaviour, not your ads. That shifts accountability from campaign managers to anyone who configures or prompts the model.
ev: Agile Brand · brand is your AI

themes.head: AI Search Creates Fragmented Engagement Signals
body: Data from adMarketplace confirms that consumers do not behave uniformly across AI search surfaces — click intent, dwell time, and conversion propensity vary significantly by experience. Treating AI search as a single channel is a planning error that will misallocate budget.

Simultaneously, ZeroRank's analysis reinforces that a citation in an AI answer is not a purchase signal. Marketers must build measurement frameworks that separate share-of-voice in AI responses from actual downstream intent and revenue.
ev: Agile Brand · adMarketplace AI search data

themes.head: AI Democratises Execution but Demands Human Context
body: Tools like GoDaddy Airo, Zakham.ai for the Middle East, and mid-market AI platforms are lowering the barrier to sophisticated marketing execution dramatically. The gap between enterprise and SMB capability is narrowing faster than most analysts predicted, with bilingual and region-specific AI workspaces accelerating global access.

Yet every practitioner piece this month echoes the same caveat: the smartest AI still fails without embedded business knowledge. Proprietary context — customer history, brand voice, pricing logic — is now the primary differentiator, not access to the model itself.

themes.head: Budget & Procurement Must Catch Up to AI Reality
body: Planning cycles are still being built around last year's martech stack while AI capability is repricing and restructuring entire categories — Mailchimp's sale to Bending Spoons being the clearest consolidation signal. What's missing from 2027 AI budgets is line-item investment in governance, data quality, and agent-readiness infrastructure rather than just tool licences.

On the procurement side, teams lack structured methods to evaluate vendor AI claims during RFPs. Vetting AI capabilities requires new criteria — model transparency, auditability, and integration depth — that standard martech scoring matrices were never designed to test.

month.takeaway: Across every corner of the feed, the month's signal is the same: AI is shifting marketing's leverage points from creative output and media placement to data ownership, agent configuration, and governance — and most budgets, teams, and procurement processes have not caught up.
